IB A3 Databases | Standard Level

SQL Worksheets

Work in sequence. The first worksheet is only about reading a schema and writing clean SELECT queries. The second moves on to sorting, pattern matching, joins, and a first grouped report. The third opens a blank workspace so students build the database themselves with DDL and DML.

Basic retrieval first Sorting and joins next Build from scratch last
Open SQL Playground Back to Unit 6

SL Coverage

  • A3.1 relational features, keys, integrity, benefits, and limitations
  • A3.2 schema reading, ERDs, data types, table structure, normal forms, and 3NF thinking
  • A3.3 SELECT, filtering, ordering, joins, plus CREATE, INSERT, UPDATE, and DELETE

Worksheet 1 | Core Retrieval

School Library

Start here. Use one clean three-table database to learn the structure of a relational model, then practise SELECT, FROM, WHERE, AND, and OR without extra SQL features getting in the way.

A3.1.1 A3.2.1 A3.3.2
Open worksheet Open dataset

Worksheet 2 | Next-Step Queries

Campus Clubs

Move here once basic filtering is secure. This worksheet assumes students already know retrieval basics and focuses on ORDER BY, DISTINCT, LIKE, BETWEEN, joins, and a first GROUP BY report.

A3.2.2 A3.2.4 A3.3.2
Open worksheet Open dataset

Worksheet 3 | Build the Database

Canteen Orders

Finish the SL sequence by building the database yourself in a blank workspace. Students work from the schema and ERD, create the tables, insert starter rows in batches, and then apply UPDATE and DELETE.

A3.2.4 A3.2.6 A3.3.1 A3.3.3
Open worksheet Open blank workspace

After SL Core

Once these three are secure, Higher Level students move to Course Enrolment for grouped calculations, views, and transactions.
